findings.title: The buyer budget could release an upto remainder without proof
findings.description: Budget reconciliation released the unspent part of an upto cap as soon as any transfer from the payer to the recipient at or below the cap appeared on chain, without proving that the transfer came from that authorization. A seller could make a session under-count what it spent and so exceed the session cap. Reconciliation now counts a payment only from a transfer made with the payment's own authorization, proven by the payer's consumed nonce.

tests: packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::settles a payment only from a transfer made with its own authorization
packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::keeps an upto remainder pending until the chain shows what moved

findings.title: Paid calls were cut off after 15 seconds of seller silence
findings.description: The SDK applied its probe's 15-second idle timeout to the paid request, although paid HTTP and MCP calls are meant to wait up to two minutes. A slow seller settled the payment and the buyer lost the answer. Paid requests now wait for the paid answer under their own timeout.

tests: packages/sdk/test/http-flow.test.ts::waits for a paid answer that takes longer than the probe's idle timeout
packages/sdk/test/mcp-flow.test.ts::waits for a paid tool that works longer than the probe's idle timeout

findings.title: A landed upto settlement could be reported as failed
findings.description: When a rebroadcast of a recorded settlement was refused as too late, the engine finished the settlement as failed with no funds moved, although the first broadcast could already have landed. The engine now keeps such a settlement pending and finishes it as failed only when the payer's unconsumed nonce proves that nothing landed.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/upto-engine.test.ts::stay pending when a rebroadcast is refused as too late: the transaction may have landed
packages/facilitator/test/upto-engine.test.ts::fail a permanently refused rebroadcast only once the unconsumed nonce proves nothing landed

findings.title: Zero-amount upto settlements were cataloged at the signed cap
findings.description: A settlement of zero under an upto authorization created or updated a Bazaar listing at the cap the buyer signed, so a listing could be published for free. Zero settlements are never cataloged.

tests: apps/rail402/test/upto.integration.test.ts::never catalogs an off-chain zero settlement

findings.title: The sponsor's hourly fee budget was optional on mainnet
findings.description: Sponsor spend on a network was bounded only by an hourly fee budget the operator could leave unset. A pubnet configuration now refuses to start without an explicit hourly budget, and the budget stops settlements before any RPC work once it is committed.

tests: apps/rail402/test/config.test.ts::requires explicit, safe mainnet settings
packages/facilitator/test/fee-exposure.integration.test.ts::stops settling once the hourly fee budget is committed, before any RPC work

findings.title: Any holder of an upto payload can choose the settled amount through /settle
findings.description: Whoever holds a signed upto payload can call /settle with any amount up to the cap before the seller does. The payer's signature still bounds the recipient, the token and the cap.

tests: apps/rail402/test/upto-settlement.integration.test.ts::lets the first settle request fix the amount: a payload holder's zero turns the seller's settle into a conflict

acceptance.rationale: The first settle request fixes the amount, as in the EVM upto scheme; the payer never loses more than the cap it signed and funds only reach the recipient it named. The documentation states this, and sellers settle as soon as they serve.
mitigations: The first settle request fixes the amount; a later request for another amount is refused as a conflict naming the original transaction.
The cap, recipient and token are bound by the payer's signature.
Mainnet facilitators can require API keys on /settle.

findings.title: A payment option without extra crashed the buyer flows
findings.description: A valid x402 v2 payment option without an extra field, or a seller error with non-string fields, raised a raw TypeError: the MCP tool reported an internal error with an unknown payment state and the CLI exited with an unexpected code. Such an option is now refused as unsponsored before anything is signed.

tests: packages/sdk/test/http-flow.test.ts::refuses an option without extra as unsponsored, in pay and in quote, before signing

findings.title: An idempotency key stayed blocked after its authorization expired unused
findings.description: Once a call with an idempotency key had no stored result, every retry with the same key was refused as in progress for the whole budget window, even after the chain showed that the authorization expired unused. The retry itself now reconciles its row and frees the key when nothing was paid.

tests: packages/sdk/test/http-flow.test.ts::frees an idempotency key on the retry itself, once the chain shows its authorization unused
packages/sdk/test/ledger.test.ts::frees a key once the chain proves its signed authorization expired unused

findings.title: Domain verification trusted a one-way claim
findings.description: A listing reached domain_verified when the host's stellar.toml listed the owner account, without the account naming the host as its home domain. An endpoint could claim another seller's account. Trust is now raised only while the domain and the account name each other.

tests: packages/bazaar/src/testing.ts::never raises trust on a one-way claim: a domain listing an account that does not name it

findings.title: Service logs could include RPC URLs and request bodies
findings.description: Transport errors from the RPC client were logged with the request URL and JSON-RPC body; a provider URL can embed an API key. The logger now writes such errors without their URL, body or headers.

tests: apps/rail402/test/logger.test.ts::logs an HTTP client error without its URL, body or headers

findings.title: Every upto verification called a public Horizon server
findings.description: The upstream upto verifier read the ledger close time from a public Horizon server on every /verify and /settle, before any static check, which made each request depend on a third party. The facilitator now reads it from its own RPC, in the service and in process.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/ledger-seconds.test.ts::reads the ledger close time from its own RPC, never from Horizon

findings.title: /health and /ready published raw internal errors
findings.description: Health warnings carried raw error strings that could include internal addresses. Public health output now names the kind of failure only; the details stay in the service log.

tests: apps/rail402/test/health.test.ts::reports an unreachable RPC and an unreadable settlement ledger

findings.title: IPv4-translated IPv6 addresses passed the destination check
findings.description: safe-fetch did not recognise the IPv4-translated range ::ffff:0:0:0/96, so a URL could reach a loopback or metadata address in that spelling. Every IP literal spelling is now classified before any lookup, and such ranges are refused.

tests: packages/safe-fetch/test/address.test.ts::classifies IP literals in every spelling before any lookup
packages/safe-fetch/test/egress.integration.test.ts::refuses IP-literal URLs to this machine in every spelling, before connecting

findings.title: An MCP paid call could exceed the request limit after signing
findings.description: Adding the payment to an MCP request could push it over the 64 KiB request limit only after the payment was signed, and the call was then reported with an unknown payment state. The size is now checked with the payment before anything is sent.

tests: packages/sdk/test/mcp-flow.test.ts::refuses a paid call that would exceed the request limit with its payment, before sending it

findings.title: A ledger failure after sending was reported as unpaid
findings.description: When the local budget ledger failed after a paid request had been sent, the SDK reported the payment as not paid and retryable, which invited a second payment. Such a call is now reported with an unknown payment state.

tests: packages/sdk/test/http-flow.test.ts::never reports a payment as unpaid when the ledger fails after it was sent

findings.title: Seller structured content was returned unsanitized
findings.description: MCP structured content from a seller was passed to the agent as received, and a __proto__ key could replace the copy's prototype. Seed redaction also missed a seed glued after other base32 characters. Structured content is now sanitized and bounded, and redaction covers glued seeds.

tests: packages/sdk/test/mcp-flow.test.ts::sanitizes structured seller content and bounds a structured payment request
packages/sdk/test/basics.test.ts::removes a seed glued after other base32 characters

findings.title: A null accepted.extra caused an unexpected error
findings.description: An upto payload whose accepted.extra was null threw inside the static rules and was answered as an unexpected error instead of a coded refusal. Such a payload is now refused with a reason naming the mismatch.

tests: packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::refuses an accepted block or accepted extra that is not an object, naming the mismatch

findings.title: An expiration margin of zero ledgers was accepted
findings.description: The upto rules require a margin of at least one ledger between the current ledger and the authorization's expiration, but the setting accepted 0. The margin now must be at least one ledger.

tests: packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::requires an expiration margin of at least one ledger

findings.title: The contract TTL keeper and channel provisioning could use the sponsor at the same time
findings.description: The keeper that extends the upto contract's TTL spent the sponsor's sequence number under a lock separate from channel provisioning, so the two could collide. Both now run under one task lock that one replica holds at a time.

tests: packages/store-postgres/test/stores.integration.test.ts::runs a named task on one replica at a time and frees the lock after it, even when it fails

findings.title: Settle-time simulation has no resource margin for smart-account payers
findings.description: A contract-account payer whose policy state grows between simulation and inclusion can make a settlement fail on chain, and the sponsor pays the fee.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/fee-exposure.integration.test.ts::names a smart account whose __check_auth passes the settle-time simulation and fails at inclusion; the fee is counted as wasted

acceptance.rationale: Not reproduced. The fee is bounded by the per-transaction fee ceiling and the hourly budget, and the failure is coded and counted as wasted fee.
mitigations: Per-transaction fee ceilings and the hourly sponsor budget bound the cost.
Failures at inclusion are reported with a stable code and counted in the wasted-fee metric.

findings.title: Rotating the upto authority breaks upto for running sellers until they restart
findings.description: A seller's resource server reads the facilitator's settlement authority once; after a rotation, its upto offers name the old authority and are refused until it restarts.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/upto-preflight.test.ts::another facilitator's authority in extra

acceptance.rationale: Rotation is a rare, planned operator action. The runbook tells operators to ask sellers to restart right after the switch; exact payments are unaffected.
mitigations: The rotation procedure in the operations guide includes the seller restart.
Refusals name the mismatch with a stable code.

findings.title: Delegated signers were never exercised end to end
findings.description: signerAuthorizations for smart accounts with delegated signers were specified and shipped but had no end-to-end test. The upto payer suite now settles with a delegate's entry and refuses a missing or forged one.

tests: apps/rail402/test/upto-payers.integration.test.ts::carries the delegate's entry in signerAuthorizations and settles

findings.title: The evidence runner passed the sponsor seed on a command line
findings.description: The conformance runbook passed the sponsor seed to env as a command-line argument, where other local users can read it. It now reads the seed from a file.

tests: tools/conformance/test/run-evidence.test.ts::never passes the sponsor seed on a command line

findings.title: A false settlement claim could hide a real payment from the budget
findings.description: A seller could report another payment's transaction hash as the settlement of a call; the claim blocked the real payment's own proof, and reconciliation then released it, so the session cap under-counted. Claims are now confirmed from the chain, never overwrite a verified settlement, and a false claim is released only after expiry.

tests: packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::confirms a reported settlement from the chain, and releases a false claim after expiry
packages/sdk/test/http-flow.test.ts::counts a reused transaction hash against each payment that reports it

findings.title: An upto settlement through a wrapper contract was released from the budget
findings.description: An upto settlement made through a wrapper or batch contract consumed the payer's nonce and moved the cap, but the proof did not recognise it and reconciliation released the row. Proofs now follow the consumed nonce, and a cap whose settled amount cannot be read is counted whole.

tests: packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::does not count an authorization carried in a transaction that never consumed it
packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::settles each payer's payment from one batch transaction in a shared ledger file
packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::counts an upto authorization's whole cap when its settlement amount cannot be read

findings.title: Rows the RPC could no longer prove stayed pending forever
findings.description: Budget rows that the RPC could no longer prove were carried into every renewed window, and the oldest ones starved reconciliation of new rows. Rows are now deferred and bounded per run, and a row is released only when the chain proves its authorization expired unused.

tests: packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::keeps a row it cannot prove pending while its authorization is still valid
packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::defers rows when the RPC fails mid-run and bounds the work per run

findings.title: A keyed MCP retry never reconciled its own row
findings.description: A retry with the same idempotency key replayed a stale error until some unrelated call reconciled the row, and MCP agents had no way to trigger it. The retry now reconciles its own row first.

tests: packages/sdk/test/mcp-flow.test.ts::frees an idempotency key on the retry itself once the chain shows its authorization unused

findings.title: An MCP tool listing could be planted under another seller for one base unit
findings.description: Paying one base unit to a seller's payTo was enough to publish and freeze an MCP tool listing with any description and price under that seller. MCP tools at an http(s) endpoint are now listed only after the tool's own server confirms them with an unpaid call, and a planted settlement can neither withdraw nor change a confirmed tool.

tests: packages/bazaar/src/testing.ts::lists an MCP tool at an https endpoint only once its unpaid call confirms it
packages/bazaar/src/testing.ts::never lets a planted settlement withdraw or change a tool its origin confirmed

findings.title: The upto reference facilitator could lose a settlement's hash
findings.description: In the reference upto mechanism, a failed send answered every repeat with an unexpected error and no transaction hash, and a pending settlement was forgotten once its authorization expired, so a landed transaction could be reported as expired. Pending settlements are now kept and polled past expiry and answered with what landed.

tests: packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::keeps polling a pending settlement after its authorization expired, and answers what landed

findings.title: The landing proof read the wrong ledger and misattributed Rail402's own settlement
findings.description: The proof that a recorded settlement landed compared a nonce read with an earlier, different RPC response, and recorded Rail402's own landed fee bump as a third-party settlement without its fee. The engine now finds its own settlement by the inner-hash lookup and attributes it correctly.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/upto-engine.test.ts::succeed as Rail402's own settlement when the inner-hash lookup finds the recorded fee bump

findings.title: The per-client rate limit keyed on full IPv6 addresses
findings.description: One IPv6 client could rotate addresses within its /64 and escape the per-client limit that bounds keyless sponsor spend. The limiter now keys an IPv6 address by its /64 and an IPv4-mapped address as the IPv4 address.

tests: apps/rail402/test/rate-limit.test.ts::keys an IPv6 address by its /64, however it is written
apps/rail402/test/rate-limit.test.ts::keys an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address as the IPv4 address

findings.title: An unknown transaction meta version read as nothing happened
findings.description: Budget proofs treated a transaction whose meta version the SDK could not decode as showing no transfer, so a future protocol upgrade could release paid rows. Such a transaction is now asked about again later.

tests: packages/sdk/test/reconcile.test.ts::asks again later about a transaction whose meta this version cannot read

findings.title: A seller that echoed the payment header put the signed payload into results
findings.description: A seller that copied the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header into its paid answer made the SDK return the signed payload in its result and store it in the budget ledger. The call's own payment material is now removed from seller content before it is returned or stored.

tests: packages/sdk/test/scrub.test.ts::removes the payment from an HTTP answer and its stored replay, keeping the rest
packages/sdk/test/scrub.test.ts::removes the payment from an MCP tool's content and structured content

findings.title: MCP listing prices were not bound when paying a listing
findings.description: When an agent paid a listed MCP tool, the live price was not compared with the listed one, so a seller could switch to a higher price up to the agent's cap. A live price above the listed one is now refused before signing.

tests: packages/sdk/test/mcp-flow.test.ts::binds a listing's price: a live price above the listed one is refused before signing

findings.title: An idempotency key reused for another resource replayed the earlier result
findings.description: A repeated idempotency key returned the earlier call's stored result even when the new call targeted a different resource or tool. Such a reuse is now refused.

tests: packages/sdk/test/http-flow.test.ts::refuses an idempotency key reused for another resource instead of replaying its result
packages/sdk/test/mcp-flow.test.ts::refuses an idempotency key reused for another tool instead of replaying its result

findings.title: Exact payments to a muxed payTo could never settle
findings.description: The stock exact verifier compares the transfer event's recipient with payTo literally, and a muxed M… address never matches the CAP-67 event, so such payments failed after submission. Exact requirements with a muxed payTo are now refused up front with a reason that names it.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/preflight.test.ts::refuses a muxed payTo, which the exact verifier cannot match to the transfer event

findings.title: A bad upto signature from a G account was reported as expired terms
findings.description: When a G payer's upto authorization was signed by a key that is not its signer, or by too few multisig keys, the simulation classifier mapped the contract's authentication error to signature_expired, telling the buyer to sign again rather than that the signature was wrong. Authentication failures now answer invalid_signature for a G payer and smart_account_rejected for a contract account; a real expiry stays signature_expired.

tests: apps/rail402/test/upto-tamper.integration.test.ts::refuses a G… payer signed with a key that is not its signer as a bad signature
apps/rail402/test/upto-tamper.integration.test.ts::refuses a 2-of-2 multisig G… payer signed with one key as a bad signature
packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::names a contract account's failed authentication as its smart account's refusal
packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::keeps the settlement contract's #5 without an authentication failure as expired terms

findings.title: A conflict was reported as final when the original settlement never reached the network
findings.description: When a request with the same authorization and another amount failed before broadcast, a concurrent request for the right amount was told the authorization was already settled, with no transaction and no retry. A request whose conflicting predecessor failed before anything reached the network is now settled.

tests: packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::settles a request whose conflicting predecessor failed before anything reached the network

findings.title: The upto fee ceiling counted the fee bump's inclusion fee once
findings.description: With a fee bump, the envelope pays the inclusion fee of the inner transaction and of the fee bump, but the ceiling check counted it once, so the sponsor could pay up to one inclusion fee above its ceiling. Both are now counted.

tests: packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::enforces the fee ceiling, counting the inclusion fee of the transaction and of its fee bump

findings.title: The upto reference facilitator could miss a settlement re-wrapped by a third party
findings.description: Confirmation polled only the outer fee-bump hash, so if a third party wrapped the public inner transaction in its own fee bump and it landed, the reference mechanism could report it as expired. It now also looks the settlement up by its inner hash.

tests: packages/upto/test/facilitator.test.ts::finds a settlement that landed inside another party's fee bump by its inner hash

findings.title: Two different maxTimeoutSeconds ranges in refusal messages
findings.description: The service named the allowed maxTimeoutSeconds range differently in two refusals. Both now name one range, raised to one ledger more than the expiration margin.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/upto-preflight.test.ts::names one maxTimeoutSeconds range, raised to a ledger more than the expiration margin

findings.title: upto events are only as trustworthy as the token contract
findings.description: A malicious token can make transfer_from do nothing and emit false events while the settlement contract still emits upto_settled, so an indexer that trusts the event alone could count a payment that never happened. The payer is not at risk.

tests: apps/rail402/test/asset-check.test.ts::fails for good, with a coded ConfigError naming the variable, when the decimals differ

acceptance.rationale: Rail402 settles only assets the operator configures per network, verifies their decimals on chain at startup, and proves transfers from the token's own events.
mitigations: Each network accepts only the assets listed in its configuration.
Asset decimals are read from the token at startup and a mismatch stops the service.

findings.title: Locked dependencies have published advisories
findings.description: The first osv-scanner and pnpm audit runs over pnpm-lock.yaml report advisories against locked versions, several rated high. Loaded at runtime by the service or the published packages: axios 1.18.0 and follow-redirects 1.16.0 (through @stellar/stellar-sdk, whose 16.x releases pin axios exactly), @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.31.0, @modelcontextprotocol/server and client 2.2.0, hono 4.13.8 and ip-address 10.7.2 (through the MCP SDK's express-rate-limit). Build and test tools only: vite 8.3.0, @vitest/mocker 5.0.1 and source-map-js 1.2.1. Each has a fixed release. Reachability: axios and follow-redirects run in the facilitator process that holds the sponsor seeds, for every RPC and Horizon call; most of the axios advisories need an attacker-chosen URL or configuration, HTTP/2 or a separate prototype-pollution primitive, and the follow-redirects ones leak credential headers when a provider redirects, which matters when an RPC URL or its headers carry a provider key; the RPC URLs are operator configuration, never request input, so exploitation needs a hostile or compromised provider, but the code is reachable and must be fixed before serving pubnet. The MCP SDK's memory-exhaustion advisory (GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453) is reachable through the public MCP endpoint of the demo seller and the MCP server's HTTP transport, which accept unauthenticated requests up to their body limit. The shared-transport advisory (GHSA-jm63-cq47-j5jp) is not reachable: both create a new transport per request. The MCP client's redirect advisory applies when the Bazaar confirms a seller's MCP endpoint, which runs through safe-fetch with redirects refused. hono's serveStatic advisory and ip-address (express-rate-limit is not used by Rail402's code) are not reachable. The development tools never run in a deployed service. The fix moves axios to 1.20.0, follow-redirects to 1.16.1, source-map-js to 1.2.2, ip-address to 10.7.4 and hono to 4.13.13 with pnpm overrides (the MCP SDK keeps its own hono otherwise), and the catalog's MCP SDK to 1.32.1, its server and client to 2.3.1, hono to 4.13.13, vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 to 5.0.5 and vite to 8.3.5 (the catalog pins vite for the browser builds, so vitest alone does not move it). With all of these, osv-scanner over every lockfile reports no advisory. The dependency scan job in CI fails while any of them is locked.

tests: tools/conformance/test/dependencies.test.ts::lock no version with a published advisory fixed in a later release
tools/conformance/test/workflows.test.ts::runs dependency scanners and pins base images by digest

findings.title: Pubnet sponsor key files lacked the network tag the service requires
findings.description: The key ceremony's tools wrote the pubnet sponsor seed without the `# rail402-key network=stellar:pubnet` tag the service requires on pubnet, so the first pubnet start would fail and invite a hand edit of the key file. The key generator now writes network-tagged key files in the service's format, with the public key printed apart.

tests: tools/conformance/test/deploy-keys.test.ts::writes network-tagged key files in the format the service reads, with the public key apart

findings.title: A dump restore left the split database roles broken
findings.description: Restoring a logical dump as the superuser left every table owned by it and took the runtime role's privileges away, so both replicas would fail their role check after an incident restore. restore-dump.sh now restores as the owner role and re-applies the runtime grants.

tests: tools/conformance/test/roles.integration.test.ts::restores a dump with the owner keeping every table and the runtime role its privileges

findings.title: No alert on WAL archiving, backup age or host disk space
findings.description: Nothing alerted when WAL archiving failed or the newest backup aged, although a failing archive fills the database's disk. Archiving, backup age and disk space are now exported for node_exporter and page the on-call.

tests: tools/conformance/test/monitoring.test.ts::watches WAL archiving, backups and host disk space, and pages on each

findings.title: A compromised facilitator could silence alerts
findings.description: The facilitator replicas shared a network with Alertmanager, whose API can create silences without authentication, so code execution in the process that holds the sponsor seed could mute every alert. The monitoring networks are now split: only Prometheus reaches Alertmanager.

tests: tools/conformance/test/monitoring.test.ts::keeps the service off the alerting network: only Prometheus reaches Alertmanager

findings.title: Recovery drills passed without checking that recovery worked
findings.description: A drill passed as soon as its alert fired; its recovery checks were recorded as text and never asserted. A drill now fails when any structured recovery check does not hold.

tests: tools/conformance/test/drills.test.ts::fail a drill whose recovery check did not hold, and keep the verdict consistent with its checks

findings.title: Alerts did not follow each network in the two-network setup
findings.description: With neither network gating /ready, an RPC outage on one network no longer raised a readiness alert, and the sponsor thresholds were not per network. Readiness is now probed per network and the thresholds are per network.

tests: tools/conformance/test/monitoring.test.ts::follows each network on its own: per-network readiness, per-network sponsor thresholds

findings.title: The deploy gate did not pin the release signer or bind the tag to origin
findings.description: The gate accepted any signature the operator's own git trust settings knew, resolved the tag locally, and accepted an attestation from any workflow or ref. Release signers are now pinned in deploy/release-signers, origin must have the same tag object, and the attestation must come from the release workflow run for that tag.

tests: tools/conformance/test/check-deployable.test.ts::refuses a tag that is not on origin, or that origin has as another object

findings.title: Alert inhibition and thresholds had the wrong semantics
findings.description: An inhibition rule treated a missing network label as equal, so any page suppressed every unrelated ticket; the budget alert tested a fixed amount instead of the share of the budget; and a replica that disappeared never alerted. Inhibition is limited to alerts with a network label, the budget ratio is used and a missing replica raises a ticket.

tests: tools/conformance/test/monitoring.test.ts::follows each network on its own: per-network readiness, per-network sponsor thresholds
tools/conformance/test/alertmanager.integration.test.ts::lets a page silence only the tickets of its own cause on its own network

findings.title: The backup documentation claimed more than the restore drill proved
findings.description: The backup section implied encryption and off-host immutability that the drill did not exercise, and pgBackRest's repository key could reach Postgres through its environment. The drill now proves the backup is encrypted, pgBackRest reads its settings from a file secret, and the documentation states what the drill does not prove.

tests: tools/conformance/test/restore-drill.integration.test.ts::records a restore drill with row counts and checksums

findings.title: Forged payloads used up the per-payTo and per-payer limits
findings.description: Payer and payTo quotas were taken before the payment proved its signatures, so anyone could exhaust a pubnet seller's or payer's quota with forged payloads at no cost. Quotas are now taken only after upstream verification and simulation succeeded.

tests: packages/facilitator/test/party-limits.integration.test.ts::forged payloads naming a payTo or a payer use none of their quota

findings.title: TTL keeper spend that failed on chain bypassed the fee budgets
findings.description: A contract TTL extension that failed on chain was never recorded, so the keeper's daily cap and the network's hourly fee budget did not see its fee. The keeper now reserves its fee ceiling before signing and corrects it to the fee charged, keeping the ceiling when the outcome is unknown.

tests: apps/rail402/test/upto-keeper-spend.integration.test.ts::keeps the ceiling counted when an extension's outcome is unknown, so the daily cap holds

findings.title: Public metrics and health revealed pubnet budget state
findings.description: The public /metrics and /health still showed when pubnet's fee budget ran out, which tells an attacker when its spend has taken effect. Pubnet budget warnings and refusal reasons are now kept off the public views.

findings.title: An exact payment with its own operation source held a channel and fee budget without landing
findings.description: The payer's authorization does not cover the operation source, and upstream settlement keeps it when it rebuilds the transaction from a channel. Because a copy of an exact authorization can still land while it is valid, a refused first submission now gives its channel back at once but stays open until the authorization expired unused (then a submission failure with nothing charged) or a copy landed (then that payment is answered); an upto settlement, which only the authority can settle, still finishes at once.

findings.title: A sequence conflict held its channel until the payment's authorization expired
findings.description: When another transaction took a channel account's sequence number, the settlement's txBadSeq refusal was treated as transient (the same bytes might have applied), so the settlement and its channel lease waited for the transaction's time bound and the payer's authorization expiry: about 4.5 minutes in the drill, with Rail402SequenceConflict firing correctly. The engine now proves the conflict final, from the channel's sequence number on the network (at least the transaction's) and the absence of the transaction's hash and inner hash at an RPC that has ingested that ledger and retains every ledger since the claim, and then finishes the settlement at once as a submission failure with nothing charged, unless the payer's nonce shows the authorization was carried elsewhere. The channel is quarantined (SETTLE_CHANNEL_QUARANTINE_MS, doubled per conflict in a row, up to 16 times) instead of being reused at once. The settlement is never re-signed on another channel, so the recorded-bytes idempotency stays as it was. An exact settlement whose bytes the network had accepted before the conflict still waits for the authorization to expire, since another transaction may carry it. For an exact settlement the proven conflict now quarantines and gives back the channel at once, while the record stays open until the payer's authorization expired unused or a copy of it landed, so a payment carried by another transaction is still answered; upto settlements still finish at once.

findings.title: The facilitator's HTTP server had no deadline for writing a response
findings.description: The service's Node server gave a response no time limit to reach its client. A client that stopped reading kept its socket and the whole response, a full discovery page included, for as long as it liked, after the request had already given up its admission slot, in the one process that settles both networks; pipelining let one connection queue many such answers. findings.title: Hourly new-listing quotas were checked only when a listing was created
findings.description: The network's and a payTo's hourly quotas of new listings counted listings when they were first cataloged. Listings created at once, or kept pending for hours while their origin did not answer, were all published together once their origin confirmed them, far past the quotas. The quotas are now spent when a listing is first published: a listing confirmed while a quota is spent waits, without spending a retry or asking its origin, until the earliest listing counted leaves the hour (publication_deferred). findings.title: A database restore could let an upto authorization settled at zero off-chain be settled again

findings.title: An upto settlement landed through another fee bump could be finished as expired on lagging RPC reads
findings.description: Once its own fee-bump hash read not found past its bounds, a settlement was finished as expired, with no funds moved, on an inner-hash lookup and a nonce read from whichever RPC answered. A lagging provider, a backend behind a balancer or another provider after a failover could answer from before the ledger at which the bounds were seen to pass, so a payment someone else's fee bump had landed was reported as expired. Reads that would prove a settlement absent, and the search for a copy after a failure on a consumed nonce, now count only from an RPC at or past the ledger their proof holds at, and with the history they need; otherwise the settlement waits. One left undecided for a minute counts in rail402_settlements_unresolvable.

findings.description: An exact transaction included and failed on chain for a cause that leaves the authorization usable (a balance spent after simulation, a trustline removed, a smart account or token that refused it for now) was finished as failed at once. The failure rolls back, nonce included, so anyone holding the payment could still land it until it expired, while the record said failed and the SDK told the buyer nothing was paid, inviting a second payment. findings.title: A contract release did not prove which revision of the third-party build workflow ran
findings.description: The contract release calls stellar.expert's reusable workflow at its main branch, which stellar.expert requires, with this repository's contents, OIDC and attestation permissions. Its only check compared that branch with the reviewed revision before the call, a second read of a mutable name, and the release's attestation was verified by signer repository alone, so a run of another revision would have gone unnoticed. The release now waits for a reviewer in the contract-release environment, and its attestation must name the reviewed workflow revision and the tag's commit (--signer-digest, --source-digest); a pubnet deploy of the upto contract checks the same revision.

findings.title: The deploy gate accepted an image built for the tag name from another commit
findings.description: The deploy gate checked that the release tag was signed and that each image's attestation came from the release workflow run for that tag name, but not that the build ran from the signed commit. Someone able to push a tag but without a release-signing key could point the tag at a commit whose own release.yml built and attested an image, then let the signed tag replace it; the gate would accept that image for the signed commit. The gate now requires each attestation to name the signed commit both as the build's source and as the workflow file that ran (--source-digest, --signer-digest).
